A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GIFT research, with matching authors, method and core experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, cross-architecture and cross-optimizer evaluations, component ablations and continual-learning results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds CDA comparisons, computational-cost measurements, label controls and optimizer diagnostics.

M1.justification: GIFT retains the same normalized soft-label and smoothed-hard-label combination followed by cosine-similarity loss. The default smoothing and mixing parameters remain 0.1, and the appendix implementation image is identical. Additional label-type experiments do not introduce a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions cover CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet-1K classification, together with Tiny-ImageNet continual learning. The new random subsets and label controls use the same source image populations and classification tasks. Higher IPC and Swin configurations extend experimental settings within this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated CDA comparisons in Table 3 and Jensen-Shannon divergence to the existing loss comparison in Table 9. The original dataset-distillation and knowledge-distillation comparators remain. Methods listed only in the new taxonomy table are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with higher-IPC CDA experiments, including ImageNet-1K IPC=200, a Swin-based RDED experiment, and runtime/peak-memory measurements. It also adds hard/smoothed-label controls on distilled and randomly sampled data, label-accuracy tracking, and learning-rate/weight-decay sweeps. The original default training configuration remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds refinement-only ImageNet ablations to Table 17, label-accuracy trajectories, additional gamma sensitivity under different augmentation, and hard/smoothed-label controls. New Appendix E investigates optimizer sensitivity through loss and gradient traces and hyperparameter sweeps. Existing continual-learning and cross-optimizer evaluations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same ± reporting practice for accuracy tables. v2 adds no stated repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or explanation of the uncertainty estimator. Additional rows and revised uncertainty values do not change that practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for CDA, Swin, computational costs and the new diagnostic experiments. It also revises the GIFT row from v1 Table 6 to v2 Table 9: for example, CIFAR-100 IPC=10 changes from 49.5 to 50.6, and ImageNet-1K IPC=10 from 21.7 to 24.0. These entries now match full-GIFT results already reported elsewhere; they do not establish a newly achieved performance gain. Main benchmark and existing cross-optimizer results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The original information-bound theorem and Appendix A proof remain unchanged. New Appendix E adds a separate mathematical analysis of SGD, Adam and AdamW, including coupled versus decoupled weight decay and an approximate parameter-shrinkage derivation under a small-gradient assumption. This substantially expands the theoretical scope without changing GIFT.

C1.justification: v2 newly presents identifying cross-optimizer generalization as a previously overlooked problem as an explicit contribution. Its abstract replaces the ordinary accuracy example with a 30.8-point cross-optimizer example recoverable from retained results. Cross-optimizer improvement itself was already claimed in v1, and the central method and performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 briefly attributes optimizer failures to KL-related gradient variance and instability. v2 replaces that account with an extended explanation involving small losses, weak task gradients and weight-decay dominance, while attributing GIFT robustness to avoiding small loss values. It also adds a shared-teacher explanation for gamma consistency and removes the conclusion's explicit image-classification limitation and proposed text/LSTM extensions.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents DATM-specific ZCA whitening, adds the CDA data-access link, reports measured training time and memory, and supplies hyperparameter values for optimizer diagnostics. These disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun. The GIFT code link, implementation image, RTX 4090 hardware and default training tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of Qin et al. on soft labels, CDA, optimizer references and references supporting approximate orthogonality. It introduces a method-selection taxonomy and positions cross-optimizer generalization as overlooked prior work. Several earlier references disappear, but the broader positioning around label utilization in dataset distillation remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much existing prose are retained. Targeted revisions foreground optimizers in the abstract and contributions, move continual learning into Appendix D, remove duplicated label-related discussion from Appendix B, and reorganize the concluding and implementation sections. Scientific additions account for much of the expansion.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial displays for CDA/Swin comparisons, computational costs, method taxonomy, label controls and diagnostic trajectories. It expands the loss-comparison and ImageNet-ablation tables, relocates continual-learning plots, and corrects the misleading captions of Figures 6 and 7. Original plot content and the implementation image are retained within the conference layout.

improvement.justification: Measured runtime and memory costs in Table 6 support the headline efficiency claim, Table 17 completes ImageNet component controls, and Table 9 resolves inconsistent GIFT entries. These improve empirical support and internal consistency. The benefit is tempered by the new optimizer explanation's unestablished implication from small loss to small gradients and removal of the explicit image-classification limitation. Overall, the revision provides a limited net quality improvement.
